deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the draft of the historical part of Riemann's Habilitationsschrift 'Über die Darstellbarkeit einer Function durch eine trigonometrische Reihe' (1854, published 1867). The page continues the story of the vibrating string. It contains no new mathematics; it restates the d'Alembert, Euler and Taylor/Bernoulli steps.

(a) D'Alembert's general solution. The string satisfies y_tt = α² y_xx (equation (1) on the previous page). Every solution has the form y = f(x+αt) + φ(x−αt). The reason given is to introduce p = x+αt and q = x−αt in place of x and t.
- Riemann's marginal computation inverts this as x = (p+q)/2 and αt = (p−q)/2.
- It then gives ∂y/∂p = ½ y_x + (1/(2α)) y_t.
- Differentiating again gives ∂²y/∂p∂q = ¼ y_xx − (1/(4α²)) y_tt.
- Hence y_tt − α² y_xx = −4α² ∂²y/∂p∂q. If this vanishes, ∂y/∂p depends on p alone, and integrating gives y = f(p) + φ(q).

(b) Fixed ends. The ends are y(0,t) = 0 and y(l,t) = 0.
- From these: f(αt) = −φ(−αt) and f(l+αt) = −φ(l−αt).
- The first gives φ(w) = −f(−w).
- Put αt = l+z in the second: f(2l+z) = −φ(−z) = f(z). This is equation (2): f is 2l-periodic.
- Substituting φ back gives equation (3): y = f(αt+x) − f(αt−x).

(c) The text then reports two historical steps:
- D'Alembert's sequel (Berlin Mém. 1747, p. 220) looks for analytic expressions invariant under z → z+2l.
- Euler (Mém. 1748, p. 69) observes that the motion is determined by the initial shape y(x,0) = g(x) and velocity y_t(x,0) = h(x), both arbitrary curves.

(d) Euler's construction of f.
- From (3) at t = 0: g(x) = f(x) − f(−x).
- Also h(x) = α(f'(x) − f'(−x)), so f(x) + f(−x) = (1/α)∫h dx (my derivation).
- These hold for 0 < x < l. Together they determine f on (−l, l), and periodicity (2) then gives f everywhere.
- The page writes the two relations with their left-hand sides interchanged (see errors).

(e) D'Alembert's objection. He insisted that y must be analytically expressible in t and x; the quotation in footnote 4 is from Mém. 1750, p. 358.

(f) Taylor's standing waves. The page writes y = sin(2nπx/l) cos(2nπαt/l), n an integer.
- This satisfies (1) and vanishes at x = 0 and x = l.
- Taylor used it to explain that a string can also sound the fundamentals of strings 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, … as long.
- He took the particular solution to be general.
- Bernoulli's superposition idea begins at the bottom of the page and continues on the next.
errors: The identity in the main text, y_tt − α² y_xx = ∂(∂y/∂(x+αt))/∂(x−αt), omits the factor −4α². The correct identity is y_tt − α² y_xx = −4α² ∂²y/∂p∂q. Riemann's own marginal computation (¼ y_xx − 1/(4α²) y_tt) gives the correct factor, and I recall (not verified) that the printed 1867 text includes the −4αα. This does not affect the conclusion y = f(p) + φ(q).
Euler's initial-value relations appear interchanged. From y = f(αt+x) − f(αt−x) one gets f(x) − f(−x) = g(x) and f(x) + f(−x) = (1/α)∫h dx. The page has + in the g relation and − in the h relation.

Taylor's modes are written sin(2nπx/l) cos(2nπαt/l). These are valid solutions but give only the even harmonics; the fundamental of a string of length l corresponds to sin(πx/l). The next page, and to my recollection the published text, use nπx/l. This is a slip, consistent with the remark about strings 1/2, 1/3, … as long.

results.what: General solution y = f(x+αt) + φ(x−αt) of the wave equation via characteristic coordinates
results.modern_name: d'Alembert's formula / characteristic coordinates for the 1D wave equation

results.what: Fixed-end conditions force φ(z) = −f(−z) and f(z+2l) = f(z), so y = f(αt+x) − f(αt−x)
results.modern_name: odd 2l-periodic extension (method of images) for the string with fixed ends

results.what: Determining f on (−l, l) from initial displacement and velocity, then extending by periodicity
results.modern_name: solution of the initial-boundary value problem by d'Alembert's formula (Euler's geometric construction)

results.what: Standing-wave particular solutions sin(kx)cos(kαt) and the harmonics of a string
results.modern_name: normal modes of the vibrating string

deep.surprise_reason: This is the historical introduction of Riemann's Habilitationsschrift, which was published in 1867. It recounts classical 18th-century results, and Riemann presents them as such.

transcription_corrections: First line: 'wie sich durch aus der identischen Gleichung' — 'durch' is a struck-out start; read 'wie sich aus der identischen Gleichung ergiebt'.
In the margin, '(3)' labels the line 'y = f(αt+x) − f(αt−x)', written beneath equation (2).
In footnote 4 the d'Alembert quotation reads 'fonction de t & de s' (s the arc length), as transcribed; it is not an error.
The marginal computation lines are better read as: ∂y/∂p = ½ ∂y/∂x + (1/(2α)) ∂y/∂t and ∂²y/∂p∂q = ¼ ∂²y/∂x² − (1/(4αα)) ∂²y/∂t².
